sections.context: Flick is 2.3k lines and about to absorb Hammerspoon, Hyperkey, an app manager, a herdr client, activity tracking, tasks and an agent bridge. Today every feature leaks into three shared places: the closed `search::Action` enum (every feature adds a variant), `app::State` (every feature adds fields and match arms in enter/refresh/render/activate), and `config::Config` (every feature adds top-level keys). Objective-C/unsafe code is spread across app.rs, ui.rs, windows.rs, spaces.rs. Each new feature would make all of these shallower and more entangled (APOSD: change amplification, cognitive load, information leakage). This refactor makes features deep, independent modules behind a narrow interface, isolates the platform, and adds a text interface (socket + CLI) so other programs and agents can compose with Flick (Unix philosophy).
sections.behavior_invariant: Everything a user can do today works identically: (1) all hotkeys in an existing config.toml (hotkey, desktop_toggle, windows_hotkey, [window_keys]) bind and behave the same, including repeat-to-cycle halves; (2) existing config.toml files parse unchanged — new per-module sections are additive, old top-level keys remain valid; (3) launcher ranking is unchanged: same fuzzy matching, same frecency, and item ids `app:<path>`, `window:<title>`, `quicklink:<name>`, `builtin:<title>` are preserved byte-for-byte so the `usage` table in an existing flick.db keeps its history; (4) clipboard history keeps its 500-clip cap, dedupe, concealed/transient skip, and paste-into-previous-app; existing `clips` rows survive; (5) window switcher order (previous window first, other-desktop apps collapsed) and desktop toggle behave the same; (6) `flick snapshot <png> [query]` and `flick import-raycast <file>` keep their arguments, output and exit codes; (7) single-instance check, Accessory activation policy, and no network access remain; (8) idle CPU stays ~0 and the release binary stays under 5 MB.
sections.approach:
Layered single crate, boundaries enforced by a check script (split into a cargo workspace only if compile times or boundary violations demand it).

Layout:
- `src/platform/` — the ONLY place with `unsafe`, objc2, Carbon, AX, CG, CF. Exposes safe, Flick-shaped functions (pasteboard, workspace, ax windows, spaces, hotkeys, timers, panel). Deep module: callers never see CF types or selectors.
- `src/core/` — pure Rust, no platform imports where avoidable: `Item`, `Ranker`/frecency, `Event`, `Module` trait, registry, `Store` (shared SQLite + per-module migrations), config loading, control protocol types. Unit-testable without AppKit.
- `src/modules/<name>/` — one directory per feature: apps, quicklinks, clipboard, windows (snap), switcher, desktop, flick (builtins). Modules depend on core + platform, never on each other.
- `src/ui/` — the panel view; renders a `ListView` and forwards keys. Knows nothing about features.
- `src/cli/` — argument parsing and the socket client.

Key interfaces (keep them small; push complexity down):
- `trait Module { fn id(&self) -> &'static str; fn items(&mut self, cx) -> Vec<Item> /* root search contributions */; fn open(&mut self, view, cx) -> Option<ListView> /* own list modes */; fn activate(&mut self, key: &str, cx) -> Outcome; fn on_event(&mut self, ev: &Event, cx) {} ; fn command(&mut self, args: &[String], cx) -> Result<String> {} /* socket/CLI verbs */ }`. Default methods do nothing, so a module implements only what it needs.
- `Item { id: ItemId { module, key }, title, subtitle, accessory, icon, keywords }` — no Action enum; activation routes to the owning module by id. `Outcome = Hide | Stay(status) | Push(ListView) | Pop`.
- `Event` enum (AppActivated, PasteboardChanged, Wake, Idle(secs), DisplaysChanged, Hotkey(binding), ...) produced by platform observers and dispatched synchronously on the main thread; background threads post to main via a channel + main-queue wakeup. No polling except where macOS forces it (pasteboard changeCount).
- Config: each module deserializes its own `[<module>]` table (with `enabled`), so module config types are private to the module. Legacy top-level keys are mapped in one place.
- Store: one connection; each module declares migrations keyed by module name in a `schema_versions` table. Modules own their tables; no cross-module SQL.
- Control socket: `~/Library/Application Support/Flick/flick.sock`, one request per line (`<module> <verb> [args...]` as JSON array), one JSON reply. `flick <module> <verb> ...` prints plain text, `--json` prints raw. `flick events` streams events as JSON lines for composition with other tools.
- Errors: one small `Error` type in core; modules surface errors as status text, never panic. Each module's event/command handlers are wrapped so a failure in one cannot take the launcher down.

Order: gates and characterization tests first, then move code without changing it (platform), then change interfaces one at a time, porting one module per step.

steps.title: Quality gates: Rust check:all (fmt, clippy pedantic subset, test, custom checks) + CI + pre-commit
Characterization tests: item ids, legacy config parsing, store schema, window rect math
Move all unsafe/objc2/CF/AX/Carbon code into src/platform with safe APIs; boundary check forbids unsafe elsewhere
Core types: ItemId-routed Item, Outcome, ListView, Module trait, registry; delete search::Action
Port features to src/modules: apps, quicklinks, clipboard, windows, switcher, desktop, flick builtins; app.rs becomes a thin view controller
Per-module config tables with enabled flag; legacy top-level keys mapped in one place
Store: shared connection, per-module migrations via schema_versions; existing usage/clips tables adopted
Event bus: platform observers (app activated, pasteboard, wake, displays, idle) dispatched to modules on main thread; panic isolation per handler
Control socket + CLI client: flick <module> <verb>, --json, flick events stream; fold snapshot/import-raycast into the same dispatcher
Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (layers, module contract, how to add a module); AGENTS.md conventions; mulch records

acceptance: Characterization tests from step 2 pass unchanged at every later step.
An existing ~/.config/flick/config.toml and flick.db load with no edits; frecency order for a fixed query matches pre-refactor.
`flick snapshot out.png ''` and `flick snapshot out.png vsc` produce visually identical PNGs before and after.
Boundary checks pass: `unsafe`/objc2 only under src/platform; no `crate::modules::` imports inside another module; no `crate::platform` imports in src/core.
Adding a toy module touches only src/modules/<toy>/ plus one registry line (verified by doing it in the docs step).
Manual smoke test on the installed app: launcher, quicklink keyword, clipboard paste, window switcher, snap + cycle, desktop toggle, reload config.
Release binary < 5 MB; idle CPU ~0% over 60 s in Activity Monitor.

name: Core: platform layer, modules, events, control socket

sections.context: Today a quicklink exists only if the user hand-edits ~/.config/flick/config.toml and runs Reload. Raycast users expect 'Create Quicklink' plus Edit/Delete on a quicklink. Flick has no way to take structured input: the only views are ListView (one search field + rows), there are no secondary actions on an item, and there is no confirmation step before a destructive action. Config is read with `toml` and the only writer (import-raycast) appends raw text. This plan adds three generic, reusable launcher capabilities (form view, per-item action menu, confirmation view), a comment-preserving config writer, and then uses them for the quicklink editor. The app manager epic (flick-7053) reuses the action menu and the confirmation view, so this plan lands its core/platform/controller steps first.
sections.approach:
Generic capabilities first, feature last. Each layer change is its own step and keeps the architecture rules: FFI only in src/platform, core pure, modules never import each other, Push-style requests by (module, name).

1. Core contract (src/core, pure, 100% coverage):
- `core::form`: `Form { module, name, title, fields: Vec<Field>, focused, submit_label, error: Option<String> }`, `Field { key: &'static str, label, value, placeholder, required: bool }`. Pure editing helpers: focus_next/prev (wrapping), set_value(index, text), value(key), missing_required().
- `core::action`: `Action { key: &'static str, title, icon: Icon, shortcut_hint: &'static str }`.
- `core::confirm`: `Confirm { module, token: String, title, lines: Vec<Item>-like rows (title, subtitle, accessory), confirm_label, destructive: bool }`.
- `Outcome::Form { module, name }` (a request, like Push, so `builtin` can open the quicklink form without importing it) and `Outcome::Confirm(Confirm)`.
- New `Module` methods with do-nothing defaults: `form(name, cx) -> Option<Form>`; `submit(&Form, cx) -> Result<String, String>` (Ok = status shown on root search, Err = inline error, form stays); `actions(&ItemId, cx) -> Vec<Action>` (computed lazily on cmd+K so state such as 'running' is fresh); `act(&ItemId, action_key, cx) -> Outcome`; `confirmed(token, cx) -> Outcome`. Registry routes each by module id; unknown module -> None/Stay(None). Not panic-isolated (same as activate).

2. Platform panel (src/platform/panel): form layout mode - a title label, up to 6 pre-created label + NSTextField rows shown/hidden per frame, an error line, footer; focus moves on Tab / Shift-Tab; a `field_changed(index)` handler and `field_value(index)` getter. New keys: `Key::BackTab` (insertBacktab:), `Key::CmdK` and `Key::CmdEnter` (via `performKeyEquivalent:` on the FlickPanel class; tail-expression returns, see mx-43d3f4). A way to make the search field read-only with a title (for confirm and action screens). Platform knows no core types: it takes its own `FormFrame` structs; callbacks are fn pointers in `Handlers` (mx-db09fc).

3. Config writer (src/config.rs + new src/config/edit.rs or src/config_edit.rs): add `toml_edit` (MIT/Apache-2.0, already allowed by deny.toml). API sketch: `config::edit_entries(module, key, op)` where op is `Append(entry) | Replace { name, entry } | Remove { name }` and entry is ordered `(field, string)` pairs. It edits the array of tables `[[<module>.<key>]]`; for Replace/Remove it also searches the legacy location from `LEGACY` (e.g. `[[quicklinks]]`) so legacy knowledge stays in config.rs. Appends always use the new table form. Comments, blank lines and key order elsewhere are byte-for-byte preserved. Writes are atomic (temp file in the same directory, fsync, rename), refuse when the file does not parse, and create the default file first if it is missing. Parses the result with `config::parse` before renaming, so a write can never leave an unloadable file.

4. UI + controller (src/ui.rs, src/app.rs, maybe new src/screen.rs): replace `view: Option<ListView>` with a `Screen` enum: Root | List(ListView) | Form(Form) | Actions { target: Item, back: Box<Screen>, items } | Confirm { confirm, back }. cmd+K on a selected row with actions opens the action list (typing filters it, Enter runs `act`, Escape returns to the previous screen with its query). Form: Tab/Shift-Tab move focus, Enter submits (missing required fields -> inline error without calling the module), Escape returns to root. Confirm: rows are read-only; non-destructive: Enter confirms; destructive: only cmd+Enter confirms, plain Enter shows 'Press ⌘↵ to <label>'; Escape cancels. Footer shows '⌘K Actions' when the selected item has actions (ask lazily; cheap). Update ARCHITECTURE.md (Module contract table, Outcome list, 'There is no Pop' paragraph) in the same commit.

5. Quicklink open-with app: `Quicklink.app: Option<String>` (app name or .app path, serde skip-if-none) and `platform::workspace::open_url_with(url, app)` via NSWorkspace openURLs:withApplicationAtURL:configuration:completionHandler: (resolve a bare name through /Applications lookups or `URLForApplicationWithBundleIdentifier`). Unknown app -> status error, not a panic.

6. Quicklink editor (src/modules/quicklinks + one builtin item): builtin item 'Create Quicklink' returns `Outcome::Form { module: "quicklink", name: "new" }`; quicklink owns forms `new` and `edit/<name>` (form names are a separate namespace from list views, so no clash with link-named views). Fields: Name (required), URL or path (required, hint '{query} for an argument'), Keyword (optional), Open with (optional app). Actions on a quicklink item: Open (primary), Edit Quicklink, Delete Quicklink, Copy URL is out of scope. Delete -> Confirm (non-destructive Enter, it only edits config). Validation (pure, unit-tested in a new validate.rs): trimmed non-empty name and URL; name unique case-insensitively (excluding the link being edited; consistent with flick-abe2); keyword has no spaces and is not used by another link; URL must contain '://' or start with '/' or '~/'. On success the module writes through the config writer and updates its own in-memory `links` (no global reload, so hotkeys are not rebound and the launcher stays open), then returns to root with 'Saved quicklink <name>'. CLI parity: `flick quicklink add <name> <url> [--keyword k] [--app a]`, `quicklink remove <name>`, `quicklink list`; `verbs()` lists them.

Parallelism: steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are independent and can run concurrently. Step 4 needs 1 and 2. Step 6 needs 3, 4 and 5.

Cross-plan ordering: this plan owns the shared action menu and confirmation view. flick-7053 (app manager) steps that add app actions and the uninstall confirmation depend on steps 1, 2 and 4 of this plan; after both plans are submitted, add `sd dep add` from those flick-7053 children to step 4's child.

Defaults chosen: 'Create Quicklink' lives in `builtin` (id `builtin:Create Quicklink`) because any `quicklink:<key>` could collide with a user's link name; this extends the pinned builtin list in src/characterization/item_ids.rs (additive behavior change, say so in the commit). Renaming a link changes its id `quicklink:<name>`, so its frecency starts over.

alternatives.name: Hand-rolled text editing of config.toml (find the [[...]] block by regex, splice lines)
alternatives.rejected_because: Fragile with inline tables, comments between keys, legacy [[quicklinks]] and multi-line strings; toml_edit is the standard format-preserving editor and reuses the same TOML grammar.

alternatives.name: Store quicklinks in SQLite (store.rs) instead of config.toml
alternatives.rejected_because: Splits the source of truth: users and import-raycast edit config.toml, and the dotfiles workflow versions it. The seed asks for config.toml.

alternatives.name: Re-serialize the whole config with toml::to_string after editing
alternatives.rejected_because: Drops every comment and reorders keys, destroying the commented default config the first run writes.

alternatives.name: Model the form as a ListView where each row is a field edited through the single search field
alternatives.rejected_because: No visible state for the other fields, awkward Tab semantics, and it cannot show labels plus values at once; a real form layout is reusable by future modules (tasks, herdr).

alternatives.name: Outcome::Form(Form) carrying the full form instead of a (module, name) request
alternatives.rejected_because: Then `builtin` would have to build the quicklink form, i.e. know quicklink fields; a request by name keeps modules independent, like Push.

alternatives.name: Finish with Outcome::ReloadConfig after every save
alternatives.rejected_because: Reload rebinds every hotkey and resets the screen; the module already knows the exact change, so updating its in-memory list is cheaper and works the same for socket commands, which cannot return an Outcome.

alternatives.name: Put the action menu and confirmation view in the app manager plan
alternatives.rejected_because: Quicklink Edit/Delete needs both too and this plan is smaller, so it can land the shared pieces sooner.

steps.title: Core: Form, Action and Confirm types; Outcome::Form/Confirm; Module form/submit/actions/act/confirmed with registry routing (pure, 100% coverage)
Platform panel: form layout (labelled text fields, focus, error line), read-only title mode, keys Shift-Tab, cmd+K and cmd+Enter
Config writer: toml_edit, comment-preserving, atomic, legacy-aware append/replace/remove of [[<module>.<key>]] entries
Controller + ui: Screen enum with form, cmd+K action menu and confirm screens; ARCHITECTURE.md contract update
Quicklink 'Open with' app: Quicklink.app field and platform::workspace::open_url_with
Quicklink editor: Create Quicklink form, Edit/Delete actions, validation, save via config writer, CLI quicklink add/remove/list

risks: ASSUMPTION: 'Create Quicklink' is a builtin root item (builtin:Create Quicklink). It changes the pinned builtin list in src/characterization/item_ids.rs; the commit must call this out as an additive behavior change. With [quicklink] enabled = false, activating it shows a status line instead of a form.
ASSUMPTION: saving updates the quicklink module's in-memory links and does not run a full config reload; a user who hand-edits config.toml meanwhile still needs Reload Flick Config.
ASSUMPTION: renaming a quicklink changes its id quicklink:<name>, so its frecency history starts over (usage table is keyed by id; no migration of usage rows).
ASSUMPTION: Delete Quicklink asks for confirmation with plain Enter (non-destructive: it only edits config). Destructive confirms (uninstall) require cmd+Enter.
ASSUMPTION: 'Open with' accepts an app name (matched like `flick app open`) or a .app path; it is stored as given.
ASSUMPTION: Edit/Delete of a link that lives in a legacy [[quicklinks]] table edits it in place there; it is not migrated to [[quicklink.links]]. New links always go to [[quicklink.links]].

cmd+K / cmd+Enter: NSTextField's field editor may consume key equivalents before the panel; performKeyEquivalent: on FlickPanel must return true only for handled keys, or system shortcuts (cmd+C/V/A in the field) break. Smoke-test copy/paste in the field.
define_class! methods cannot early-return false (mx-43d3f4); use tail expressions in performKeyEquivalent:.
app.rs is 321 lines; the Screen enum and three new screens can push it over the 500-line check:size budget. Put pure screen state/transition code in a new file (mx-e7e3ab); never raise a budget.
Core coverage floor is 100% (scripts/coverage-budgets.json 'src/core/'); every new core branch needs a unit test.
toml_edit adds a second TOML parser to the binary; check:binary-size ceiling is 5 MB and the release binary is ~3.7 MB. Disable default features not needed (e.g. keep only 'parse' and 'display').
Atomic rename replaces a symlinked config.toml with a regular file. Resolve the symlink (fs::canonicalize) and write next to the target; dotfile setups often symlink it.
A write that races a hand edit loses one of them; re-read and parse the file immediately before editing, never cache the document.
Panel focus: switching between the search field and form fields must keep the panel key window; windowDidResignKey hides the launcher, so never make a non-panel window key.
Modules never import each other: builtin opens the form only through Outcome::Form { module: "quicklink", name: "new" }; check:layers enforces it.
acceptance: scripts/check-all.sh passes after every step; no file-size, coverage or binary-size budget is raised.
src/core coverage stays 100%; unit tests cover Form focus wrap, required-field detection, registry routing of form/submit/actions/act/confirmed to the owning module, and unknown-module fallbacks.

Config writer tests: on DEFAULT_CONFIG plus a hand-commented fixture, Append/Replace/Remove change only the targeted entry (diff of the rest of the file is empty); comments and blank lines survive; Replace/Remove find an entry under legacy [[quicklinks]]; a write whose result would not parse is refused and leaves the file untouched; a symlinked config is written through to its target.
Validation tests: empty name, empty URL, duplicate name (any case), keyword with a space, keyword used by another link, editing a link keeps its own name/keyword valid.

`flick quicklink add Docs https://docs.rs/{query} --keyword d` exits 0, appends a [[quicklink.links]] entry, and `d serde` in root search opens immediately without a reload; `flick quicklink add Docs x` fails with a duplicate-name error and exit 1; `flick quicklink remove Docs` removes it; `flick help` lists the new verbs.
ARCHITECTURE.md documents Outcome::Form, Outcome::Confirm, the new Module methods and the Screen behavior (action menu Escape returns to the previous screen) in the same commit as step 4.
Existing characterization tests pass unchanged, except the builtin id list in item_ids.rs, which gains 'builtin:Create Quicklink' (commit message says so).

Manual smoke (installed app): (1) type 'create quick', Enter -> form with 4 fields, focus in Name; (2) Tab/Shift-Tab cycle fields; Enter with empty URL shows an inline error; (3) fill Name 'Crates', URL 'https://crates.io/search?q={query}', Keyword 'cr', Enter -> back at root with 'Saved quicklink Crates'; 'cr tokio' opens crates.io; (4) select Crates, cmd+K -> Edit/Delete actions; Edit shows prefilled values; change keyword to 'crt', save, 'crt x' works and 'cr x' no longer does; (5) cmd+K -> Delete -> confirm screen, Escape cancels (link still there), repeat and Enter -> link gone; (6) config.toml comments unchanged (git diff / diff against a copy shows only the edited entry); (7) a link with Open with 'Safari' opens in Safari while another browser is default; (8) cmd+C / cmd+V / cmd+A still work in the search field and in form fields; (9) Escape from the form returns to root; the launcher hotkey toggles as before; (10) Reload Flick Config still works after edits.

name: Forms, action menu, confirm; quicklink editor

sections.context: The app module only lists installed apps and opens them (src/modules/apps/mod.rs). Quitting, force-quitting, revealing in Finder and uninstalling all mean leaving the launcher for Finder, Activity Monitor or a third-party uninstaller (AppCleaner). Flick should do these from an app item, like Raycast. Uninstall is the risky part: deleting the wrong path loses user data. So it must move items to the Trash (recoverable, never rm), show exactly what will go before anything happens, find leftovers conservatively (bundle-id names only, inside a fixed set of ~/Library folders), and refuse system apps. This plan builds on the generic action menu (cmd+K) and confirmation screen delivered by the flick-32a7 plan.
sections.approach:
Prerequisite (cross-plan): the flick-32a7 plan must land its steps 1 (core Action/Confirm + Module actions/act/confirmed), 2 (panel keys cmd+K, cmd+Enter) and 4 (controller action menu and confirm screens) before steps 4 and 5 here start. After both plans are submitted, run `sd dep add <this plan's step-4 child> <flick-32a7 step-4 child>` and the same for step 5. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 6 here do not need the other plan.

All new FFI goes in src/platform; everything else is in src/modules/apps (split into files to stay under 500 lines: mod.rs, actions.rs, running.rs, leftovers.rs, uninstall.rs). Item ids stay `app:<bundle path>` (pinned).

1. Platform app control (src/platform/workspace.rs, new fns): `bundle_id(path) -> Option<String>` (NSBundle bundleWithPath / bundleIdentifier), `running_for_bundle(path) -> Vec<i32>`, `terminate(pid) -> bool` (NSRunningApplication terminate: polite, like cmd+Q, the app may ask to save), `force_terminate(pid) -> bool` (forceTerminate), `reveal(path)` (NSWorkspace activateFileViewerSelectingURLs). Expose Flick's own bundle path from platform::app so the module can protect itself.
2. Platform trash (new src/platform/files.rs): `trash(path) -> Result<PathBuf, String>` using NSFileManager trashItemAtURL:resultingItemURL:error:, returning the item's new location in the Trash; the NSError's localized description becomes the Err text. No other delete primitive is added anywhere.
3. Pure leftovers + protection (src/modules/apps/leftovers.rs, no platform calls; home dir and bundle id are parameters so tests use a temp dir): roots are exactly ~/Library/{Application Support, Caches, Preferences, Containers, Group Containers, Saved Application State, LaunchAgents, Logs, HTTPStorages, WebKit}. Matching is exact on the bundle id `bid`: `<bid>` (any root), `<bid>.plist` (Preferences, LaunchAgents), `Preferences/ByHost/<bid>.<hardware-uuid>.plist`, `<bid>.savedState` (Saved Application State), `<bid>.binarycookies` (HTTPStorages), and in Group Containers `<TEAMID>.<bid>` or `group.<bid>`. Case-sensitive. No prefix matching (com.google.Chrome must not match com.google.Chrome.canary), no app-name matching. Entries are read with symlink_metadata: symlinks are never followed and a symlink entry is skipped; every result must be a direct child of an allowed root (or of Preferences/ByHost) after canonicalizing the root. Sizes are summed with a non-following walk. `protected(app_path, bid, own_bundle) -> Option<reason>`: path under /System or /Library/Apple, bid empty or starting with `com.apple.`, Flick itself, or a path outside /Applications, ~/Applications and their one-level subfolders. Add a 100% (or measured) floor for this file to scripts/coverage-budgets.json (tightening only).
4. App actions (src/modules/apps/actions.rs) via `Module::actions`/`act`: Open Application (primary Enter, unchanged), Show in Finder, Quit (only when running), Force Quit (only when running), Uninstall… (hidden for protected apps). CLI: `app quit <name>`, `app force-quit <name>`, `app reveal <name>`; update `verbs()`.
5. Uninstall (src/modules/apps/uninstall.rs): Uninstall… computes the plan (app bundle + leftovers + sizes) and returns `Outcome::Confirm` with destructive = true: title 'Uninstall <App>', one read-only row per path with its size, a total, and confirm label 'Move N items (X MB) to Trash'; only cmd+Enter confirms. The module stores the exact list under the confirm token; on `confirmed` it trashes exactly that list (re-checking each path is still an allowed match and still exists; changed paths are skipped and reported). The app bundle is trashed first; if that fails, nothing else is touched. Leftover failures do not stop the others; the status line reports counts and the first error. A running app is refused ('Quit <App> first'). Afterward the app index rescans. CLI: `app uninstall <name> --dry-run` prints `<size>\t<path>` lines and a total, exit 0; `app uninstall <name> --yes` performs it and prints what moved; with neither flag it prints the list and fails ('pass --yes to move these to the Trash'), exit 1.
6. Running Applications view (src/modules/apps/running.rs): a root item 'Quit Applications' (id `app:quit` - safe because app keys are absolute paths starting with '/') opens view `app/running` listing running regular apps (platform::workspace::regular_apps) with their icons; Enter quits the selected app (id `app:<path>` with arg 'quit'), cmd+K gives the step-4 actions (Force Quit etc.). The view refreshes on `AppActivated` events. CLI `app running` prints `<pid>\t<name>\t<path>`. The existing `app list` covers the installed-app list.

Parallelism: steps 1, 2 and 3 can run concurrently (and concurrently with all of flick-32a7). Step 6 needs only step 1. Step 4 needs step 1 plus flick-32a7 step 4. Step 5 needs 2, 3 and 4 plus flick-32a7 step 4. Steps 5 and 6 can run concurrently.

alternatives.name: Delete with std::fs::remove_dir_all / rm
alternatives.rejected_because: Unrecoverable; one wrong match destroys user data. The Trash keeps every uninstall reversible and the seed requires trashItemAtURL.

alternatives.name: AppCleaner-style fuzzy matching (app name, vendor name, bundle-id prefixes)
alternatives.rejected_because: Finds more leftovers but also other apps' data (Chrome vs Chrome Canary, 'Code' folders). Conservative exact bundle-id matching was requested; missed leftovers are harmless, wrong ones are not.

alternatives.name: Scan /Library (system-wide) and privileged helpers too
alternatives.rejected_because: Needs admin rights and touches other users' data; out of scope. Only the user's ~/Library roots listed in the seed.

alternatives.name: Quit the app automatically before uninstalling
alternatives.rejected_because: Quitting can lose unsaved work and the app may refuse; refusing with 'Quit <App> first' keeps the destructive flow to one explicit decision.

alternatives.name: Plain Enter to confirm uninstall
alternatives.rejected_because: Enter is the key the user just pressed to choose Uninstall…; a double press would trash data. cmd+Enter makes the destructive confirm a deliberate, different key.

alternatives.name: A separate 'manage apps' module
alternatives.rejected_because: It would duplicate the app index and could not import the apps module; the features act on app:<path> items, so they belong to the app module.

steps.title: Platform: bundle id lookup, running pids per bundle, terminate/force-terminate, reveal in Finder, Flick's own bundle path
Platform: files::trash via NSFileManager trashItemAtURL (the only delete primitive)
Apps: pure leftover finder (exact bundle-id matches in the ~/Library roots, no symlinks, sizes) and system-app protection, with temp-dir tests
Apps: action menu on app items (Show in Finder, Quit, Force Quit) + CLI app quit/force-quit/reveal (needs flick-32a7 step 4)
Apps: Uninstall with confirm screen (paths + sizes, cmd+Enter), trash exactly the listed paths, CLI app uninstall --dry-run/--yes (needs flick-32a7 step 4)
Apps: Quit Applications view of running apps (Enter quits) + CLI app running

risks: ASSUMPTION: leftovers are exact bundle-id names only; folders named after the app (e.g. ~/Library/Application Support/Slack) and bundle-id-prefixed helpers (com.foo.App.helper) are not found. Some data stays behind; this is the conservative trade-off.
ASSUMPTION: uninstalling a running app is refused with 'Quit <App> first'; it is not quit automatically.
ASSUMPTION: destructive confirmation needs cmd+Enter (plain Enter shows a hint); Escape cancels. The CLI needs --yes to act, --dry-run only lists.

ASSUMPTION: protected = anything under /System or /Library/Apple, any com.apple.* bundle id, apps with no bundle id, Flick itself, and apps outside /Applications and ~/Applications (plus one subfolder level, matching the scan). Protected apps show no Uninstall action and the CLI refuses them.
ASSUMPTION: no privilege escalation. Root-owned or App Store apps that the user cannot trash fail with the system's error text ('use Finder'); leftovers are then untouched.
ASSUMPTION: 'list' is covered by the existing root items and `app list`, plus the new Quit Applications view and `app running`; no separate installed-apps manager view.

Cross-plan dependency: steps 4 and 5 cannot start until flick-32a7 steps 1, 2 and 4 are merged (Module::actions/act/confirmed, cmd+K/cmd+Enter, controller screens). Add the sd deps after submitting both plans.

Containers and Group Containers are protected by macOS (App Management / container privacy on macOS 14+); trashItemAtURL can fail or trigger a TCC prompt. Report per-path failures; never retry with another delete method.

A confirm token that outlives a change (app updated, leftover replaced by a symlink) could trash something not shown: re-validate every stored path against the same matching rules and symlink_metadata just before trashing, skip and report any that changed.

Sizing a large Containers folder can take seconds on the main thread and freeze the launcher. Cap the walk (e.g. stop at 200k entries and show '>= X') or compute in a background thread and post the confirm back with platform::events::on_main (mx-1d2d92); never touch module state off-main.
Bundle id lookup per app during scan() on every LauncherOpened would slow the launcher; look it up lazily (on cmd+K / uninstall), not in scan().
Quit (terminate) is asynchronous and can be vetoed by the app; report 'Asked <App> to quit', not 'Quit'. Force Quit loses unsaved data: show it only for running apps and label it clearly.

Item id format app:<path> and the pinned root ordering in src/characterization must not change; the 'Quit Applications' root item (app:quit) extends the app items — check ranking/item_ids characterization tests and call out any changed assertion in the commit.
check:size: apps/mod.rs is 141 lines today; keep new code in separate files. Coverage floors only tighten.
acceptance: scripts/check-all.sh passes after every step; no budget raised; check:layers shows no unsafe/objc2 outside src/platform and no cross-module imports.
grep shows no remove_file/remove_dir/remove_dir_all/`rm` in src/modules/apps or src/platform/files.rs; platform::files::trash is the only removal path used by uninstall.

Leftover finder unit tests (temp HOME): for bid dev.flick.test it finds Caches/dev.flick.test, Preferences/dev.flick.test.plist, Preferences/ByHost/dev.flick.test.<UUID>.plist, Saved Application State/dev.flick.test.savedState, HTTPStorages/dev.flick.test.binarycookies, Group Containers/ABCDE12345.dev.flick.test, LaunchAgents/dev.flick.test.plist; it ignores dev.flick.test2, dev.flick.test.helper, DEV.FLICK.TEST, a folder named after the app, a symlink named dev.flick.test pointing outside ~/Library, and anything in ~/Library roots not on the list; sizes match the bytes written.

Protection unit tests: /System/Applications/Safari.app, any com.apple.* bid, Flick's own bundle, a bundle without bid and /usr/local/foo.app are protected; /Applications/Foo.app with dev.foo.bar is not.

`flick app uninstall <name> --dry-run` lists exactly the bundle plus matched leftovers with sizes and a total and changes nothing on disk; without flags it exits 1 with the list and the --yes hint; `flick app uninstall Safari --dry-run` fails as protected.
`flick app quit|force-quit|reveal <name>` and `flick app running` work and appear in `flick help`.

Manual smoke (installed app) with a fixture: make ~/Applications/FlickTest.app (minimal Info.plist, CFBundleIdentifier dev.flick.uninstall-test, an executable stub), and create ~/Library/Caches/dev.flick.uninstall-test/, ~/Library/Preferences/dev.flick.uninstall-test.plist, ~/Library/Saved Application State/dev.flick.uninstall-test.savedState/, plus a decoy ~/Library/Caches/dev.flick.uninstall-test-other/. (1) Open launcher, type 'FlickTest', cmd+K shows Open / Show in Finder / Uninstall…; (2) Show in Finder reveals the bundle; (3) Uninstall… shows a confirm screen listing exactly the 4 real paths with sizes and the total, not the decoy; (4) Enter alone does nothing but show the cmd+Enter hint; Escape cancels and all files still exist; (5) Uninstall… again, cmd+Enter -> status 'Moved 4 items … to Trash'; all 4 are in ~/.Trash (Put Back works in Finder), the decoy still exists, FlickTest no longer appears in search; (6) Safari, Finder and Flick show no Uninstall action; (7) with TextEdit open and an unsaved document, Quit asks to save, Force Quit (from the Quit Applications view via cmd+K) terminates it; (8) Quit Applications view lists running apps and updates when an app launches; Enter quits the selected app; (9) launcher hotkey, root search ranking and app opening behave as before.
